title: Police Searched Illegally — Can They Still Use It? #Shorts
description:
Police search a home illegally and find something. Can they still use it against you?

In 1957, officers forced their way into a woman's house without a valid warrant. The suspect they were after wasn't there. Instead, they found some books — and charged her with a different crime.

In 1961, in Mapp v. Ohio, the Supreme Court ruled that evidence from an illegal search can't be used in court — in any state. Sometimes a guilty person goes free, because the police broke the rules.

Watch the full story on the channel.

#Shorts #MappVOhio #SupremeCourt #FourthAmendment #ExclusionaryRule #Law #Documentary
